A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UP2You and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated material can be matched reliably, supporting comparison of the complete papers.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on PuzzleIOI, 4D-Dress, and collected in-the-wild photographs, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds component ablations, reconstruction comparisons, and qualitative robustness and animation results.

M1.justification: The PCFA aggregation procedure, perceiver shape predictor, RGB/normal generators, losses, and mesh reconstruction pipeline are retained. The default feature-selection parameter γ = 2.0 was already specified in v1 Appendix D.1. New architecture and encoder alternatives are evaluated as ablations, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training and benchmark datasets remain unchanged. V2 adds qualitative scenarios with entire body regions absent from all references, loose clothing combined with complex target poses, and an animation demonstration (Figures 12–13, 21, 24, and 29), modestly extending tested conditions.

E2.justification: V2 Table 8 adds evaluated reconstruction comparisons with ICON, ECON, PIFuHD, and Human3Diff alongside PSHuman. Table 2 adds an MLP shape predictor, and Table 6 compares CLIP and DINOv1 against DINOv2 specifically as PCFA correlation encoders. Existing album-reconstruction baselines remain.

E3.justification: Original splits, training budgets, reference-count settings, and metric definitions are retained. Added protocols include a γ = 1, 2, 3 sweep and Table 8's comparison of multi-reference UP2You with single-front-view baselines, reporting front and back appearance metrics separately.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of shape-predictor architecture, the PCFA correlation encoder, and selected-feature count, plus missing-region and difficult-pose case studies. These address several previously untested design and robustness questions. Original pose-consistency and shape-predictor analyses are retained in Appendix F, rather than removed.

E5.justification: The existing mean/variance reporting for single-input shape predictors is retained. Added results introduce no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results through Tables 6–8, the MLP column in Table 2, and qualitative stress tests and animation examples. For example, the new MLP result at 12 references is V2V 8.336 versus the retained UP2You value 7.399. Original Tables 1 and 3–5 and relocated pose/shape results retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), the SMPL-X and feature-aggregation definitions, and Appendix D.3's training losses are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same data-rectifier contribution, PCFA and shape-prediction claims, reported accuracy improvements, 1.5-minute reconstruction time, and pose-control/virtual-try-on capabilities. The shortened conclusion preserves this scope; added experiments primarily support existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains that completely unseen body regions may receive hallucinated structure and textures blended from visible regions, recommending complete body coverage. Appendix E.3 newly cautions that independently reconstructed animation frames lack guaranteed temporal and mesh-topology consistency. Existing limitations are retained in Appendix H.

D1.justification: V2 removes the title-page project URL and adds brief output-animation guidance involving Mixamo and skin-weight transfer. Appendix D's architecture, data preparation, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and inference details remain unchanged. Both abstracts still promise future code and model release.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning DINOv1, CLIP, FoundPose, Human-3Diffusion, Mixamo, and skin-weight transfer, and removes the continuous-remeshing reference. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against personalization/SDS approaches remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: the standalone application discussion is condensed into the conclusion, limitations move to Appendix H, and detailed pose/shape analyses move into an expanded Appendix F. New animation and robustness discussions are integrated, while introductory and methodological prose remains largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three quantitative tables, an MLP column, and multiple robustness and animation figures. Pose and reference-count visualizations gain panels, including intermediate 6- and 9-reference results. Existing inference, shape-analysis, try-on, and limitation displays are relocated or repacked extensively.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evidence for component choices and clarifies missing-region and animation limitations, providing a modest quality gain over v1's already substantial evaluation. Core results remain unchanged. The new Table 8 offers qualified support: methods receive different input information, and PSHuman's front-view PSNR exceeds UP2You's (25.384 versus 25.257), tempering the accompanying broad superiority wording.
